clue.text: They're essential. Am I?

definitions.meaning: essential components, the basic building blocks of anything
Am (americium) and I (iodine) are chemical symbols, so the pair are examples of what is asked for

explanation.walkthrough: 'Am I?' looks like a doubting question, but read Am and I as chemical symbols: each stands for a chemical substance in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic constituents are things essential to a whole, and americium and iodine are entries in the periodic table.

clue.text: Real Charlie's in the ascendant

indicators.note: in a down clue something ascendant rises, so the letters are read from bottom to top
Charlie sits inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A claim that the genuine Charlie is on the rise in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside THE to make THCE; 'in the ascendant' then turns that upwards, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-derived word means genuine or authentic, a borrowing used in English for the real thing.

clue.text: Discern the essence of Bernie's pyramid!

indicators.note: the essence is the inner core, so the letters are found inside the words Bernie's pyramid

explanation.surface: An exhortation to perceive what Bernie's pyramid is really about.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join: bernieS PYramid.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or make out, a synonym of discern.

clue.text: Volcano's showing changes, to be sure

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that a volcano certainly displays alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sure' reads as a phrase, but only BE SURE is rearranged; 'changes' is the signal and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Erebus is an active volcano in Antarctica, named after one of Ross's ships.

clue.text: Indonesia, a country beset by terror, shows an empirical approach

indicators.note: the first pieces are surrounded by the word terror, as a country beset by enemies is hemmed in

parts.note: taken as written
RI is the international vehicle registration code for Indonesia
taken as written
a country is a land

explanation.surface: A news item about an Asian nation besieged by terrorism showing a practical approach.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of Indonesia's code, the article and the nation sit after the first letter of the frightening word; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying things and learning from failures is an experimental, evidence-based method rather than a theoretical one.

clue.text: Looks carefully at policeman in corner of London square

indicators.note: the policeman is placed inside the London corner

parts.note: SE is the south-east, a corner of London as a postal district
a cop is a policeman
S is taken as an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: A constable keeps an eye on things from a corner of a London square.
explanation.walkthrough: A corner of London means a compass-point district such as the south-east, not a street corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To scope something out, or scope it, is informal for examining or inspecting it closely.

clue.text: Franciscan primate

definitions.meaning: a friar of a branch of the Franciscan order, named for the pointed hood
a South American monkey with a cap of hair resembling a friar's cowl

explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' tempts as an archbishop alongside a churchman, but here it is a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The friars' order gave its name to the monkey, whose head colouring recalls their hood.

clue.text: Forecast to prince: Di is unstable

indicators.note: something unstable will not hold its shape, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning to Prince Charles that Diana is volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what will happen, a synonym for a foretelling.

clue.text: Way of riding is rejected, having finally destroyed knee joint

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the last letters of the two words destroyed and knee

parts.note: a saddle is a joint of meat, the back cut of lamb or mutton

explanation.surface: A grim report about a horse rider whose knee has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' serves both destroyed and knee, giving two final letters; 'joint' is the butcher's cut, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding with both legs on one side of the horse was the traditional style for women in skirts.

clue.text: Fashionable event

definitions.meaning: trendy and lively, the place where things are going on
an occurrence, especially an improvised public performance

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means trendy; as a noun it means an occurrence or improvised show.

clue.text: A dragoman is to translate for a kind old Palestinian

indicators.note: to translate is to turn into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request that an interpreter render words for a charitable figure of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman is an interpreter in the Middle East, which makes 'translate' sit naturally; 'to' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable of a charitable man from Samaria, an ancient region of Palestine, gave English this phrase for a helpful stranger.

clue.text: Inner Temple advocates speak in court

indicators.note: the word inner says the letters lie inside the words Temple advocates

explanation.surface: Lawyers at a London Inn of Court argue before judges.
explanation.walkthrough: Inner Temple is one of London's four Inns of Court for barristers, so 'Inner' looks like part of the name; the letters span temPLE ADvocates.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to present a case or answer a charge before a judge.

clue.text: They hold together Oxonian official's cuffs

parts.note: at Oxford University a bulldog is a proctor's attendant, a minor official
to cuff is to clip, hit with the hand

explanation.surface: An Oxford university official's hits on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuffs' suggests the ends of sleeves or handcuffs, but it is a verb or noun for blows: CLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring-loaded metal clips grip sheets of paper and keep them together.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom's gang discovered a way of making you talk?

definitions.text: a way of making you talk?

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of folk tales, so Tom may suggest Thumb's
a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a folk hero's gang uncovered a method of interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A torture device that crushes the digits was used to extract confessions.

clue.text: Enjoying things together and beginning to develop trust

parts.note: shared enjoyment is mutual fun

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word develop

explanation.surface: An account of a friendship growing through shared pleasures and confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trust' seems to be part of the relationship, but it is the financial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment trust pools money from many investors, which is what this kind of fund does.

clue.text: Plunder stateroom

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Plunder stateroom', runs 'state room' together: the homophone indicator 'state' and HALL ('room') share one word, so it cannot be parsed honestly.

clue.text: Making Susie stand alone

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Encouraging a child called Susie to stand by herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unaided means doing it alone, without help.

clue.text: Entire league participates in contest

indicators.note: the league letter takes part inside the contest word

parts.note: to contest is to compete

explanation.surface: A whole sports league joins a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complete is whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Goldfish buried in mummies' tombs

indicators.note: the goldfish letters are put inside the word for mothers

parts.note: mummies are mothers, mums
gold is AU, its chemical symbol, and the fish is a sole

explanation.surface: Pet fish laid to rest among the wrappings of Egyptian burial chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldfish' splits as gold (AU) and fish (SOLE); 'mummies' means mothers, not Egyptian bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Large stately tombs are named after that of Mausolus at Halicarnassus.

clue.text: Oversized device?

parts.note: split the first word as over plus sized: over means too and the size label for large is L, and the whole is an implement

explanation.walkthrough: Clothing labels mark large size with L, so 'Oversized' hints at too large; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: The joke spelling of too-large lands on a general word for an implement or instrument.

clue.text: Long to join a student organ

parts.note: to long for is to pine
taken as written
L, the learner plate, stands for student

explanation.surface: Wanting to sign a student up to an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineal gland is a small endocrine organ in the brain.

clue.text: Model sat for triple likeness

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are remodelled into a new form

explanation.surface: A model posed to have a picture painted three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the sitter but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the artist by the artist is a likeness of the painter.

clue.text: Fail to take advantage of girl

definitions.meaning: to let an opportunity pass by unused
a title for, and so a word for, a young unmarried woman

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means failing to seize a chance; the noun is a title and term for a young woman.

clue.text: Male friend's about to become a Muslimofficial

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ami is French for a male friend

explanation.surface: A man's pal is about to take up a religious post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns M + AMI (MAMI) round; the clue as held runs 'Muslim official' together.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of prayers in a mosque, or a Muslim religious leader, holds this title.

clue.text: In those days international unit included unusual, singular1 across

indicators.note: the time and unit letters are included inside the strange word

parts.note: rum means odd or unusual
then means at that time
IU is the abbreviation for international unit

explanation.surface: A tangle of historical units forms one of the opening answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' turns the plural first across answer into one of them; the clue as held prints '1 across' as 'singular1 across'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthenium is a metallic element, one member of the periodic table.

clue.text: Wife and I had to buy a gizmo

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
to get something is to buy it

explanation.surface: A husband explains that his wife and he had to purchase a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is a small unnamed gadget or mechanical device.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom meets South American in America

parts.note: Uncle Tom is one example of an uncle, from the novel
SAm is an abbreviation for South American

explanation.surface: A man named Tom meets a South American visitor in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America' looks like a place; it is the definition, as the national personification.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in stars and stripes personifies the US government and the nation.
